description: File one or more bugs you found but are not fixing, as a set. Opens a report and publishes each issue as its own guide — its own id, share link, and verdict — so a reviewer can hand any one of them to whoever fixes it. Use this after a test run, a QA pass, or a review that turned up defects; use publish_guide instead for work you finished and want repeated elsewhere. If there is a screenshot of any of this, it is evidence: call attach_screenshot first and pass what it returns as that issue's `evidence`. Describing a screenshot instead of attaching it throws away the most useful thing in the report. Needs sync (`passalong login`).

cwd.description: directory the bugs were found in

environment.description: production, staging or development — where you saw these

issues.description: one entry per defect; file them together rather than one call each

area.description: which surface it is on — known: web, mobile, storefront, landing, auth

evidence.description: screenshot URLs from attach_screenshot, or the markdown lines it returned; they go under Problem, where a reader looks first

gotchas.description: anything already ruled out, or that made it hard to pin down

problem.description: what is broken and what it stops someone doing; the error if there is one

reproduce.description: numbered steps that show the bug — these produce it, they are not a fix

severity.description: s1 blocker, s2 major, s3 minor, s4 cosmetic (default s3)

summary.description: one or two plain sentences for a PERSON, no ids or paths: what is broken and whether anyone needs to act. Defaults to the title

title.description: what is broken, in one line

verification.description: the behaviour that should have happened, as something a fixer can check

title.description: what the sweep was, e.g. "Checkout regression pass, 8 Sep build"

to.description: team slug, team/@handle for one teammate, team/@ada,@bola for several named teammates, or team/#group for a set of them

name: file_bugs
title: File bugs
